newsitem.title: USA: Columbia posts strong Q2 despite troubles.
newsitem.headline: Columbia posts strong Q2 despite troubles.

text.p: Despite management upheaval and a government probe of its business, Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp reported Wednesday that it continues to outperform industry growth trends.

For the second quarter, the largest U.S. for-profit hospital company reported revenues of $5.2 billion and net profit of $412 million, compared to year-earlier revenues of $4.9 billion and net profit of $364 million.
In line with Wall Street expectations, second-quarter earnings per share rose to $0.62 from $0.54 a year ago.
Same-facility net revenues grew six percent, based on same-facility adjusted admissions growth of five percent and same-facility inpatient admissions growth of three percent, the company said.

Columbia shares were off 4/16 to 34-1/16 in early New York Stock Exchange trading. Analysts said the stock was likely to drift in the low to mid-30s until some resolution is reached in the government investigation.
For the six months ended June 30, Columbia revenues totaled $10.5 billion, up from $9.9 billion a year earlier. Earnings per share rose to $1.32 from $1.15.
Columbia said it expects to close its Value Health Inc purchase "as soon as regulatory matters concerning the State of California Department of Corporations are resolved."
Columbia also said it had decided not to proceed with a previously announced letter of intent to acquire a majority interest in America's Health Network.
Various federal agencies is looking into Columbia's laboratory billing, home healthcare and Medicare-related business practices.
Investigations of the company are also being conducted by the attorneys general of Texas and Alabama.
Long-time Columbia Chief Executive Richard Scott resigned Friday, along with President David Vandewater. Dr. Thomas Frist, formerly vice chairman, was named chairman and chief executive.
Columbia historically has enjoyed same-hospital revenue growth of 7 to 11 percent year-over-year, versus the industry average of about 5 percent.
The company has typically reported same-hospital admissions growth of 2 to 5 percent, also above the industry average, said analysts.
